rows.label: AB 1482 SF state-only cap
rows.notes: Does NOT apply to units under SF Rent Ordinance limits.

rows.label: State cap formula
rows.value: 5% + CPI or 10% lower; max two increases/12 months
rows.notes: CPI-U April-over-April, rounded nearest 0.1%, Aug. 1 cutoff.

rows.label: More-restrictive local exemption
rows.value: Units already subject to more restrictive local rent control are exempt from state cap
rows.notes: Local protections remain.

rows.label: Just cause
rows.value: Required after 12/24 months; lease expiration alone is not just cause
rows.notes: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rows.label: Notice
rows.value: 30 days <=10%; 90 days >10%; 827(c) longer notice controls
rows.notes: Personal delivery/mail rules.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins initial rent
rows.value: No limit on initial rent for vacant unit
rows.notes: Not a reset for existing tenancy.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins d(2)
rows.value: Unlimited increase only to qualifying post-1995 lawful sublessee/assignee after original occupants no longer permanently reside
rows.notes: Co-tenants excluded.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins d(3)
rows.value: Partial occupancy changes protected when original occupant or qualifying pre-1996 lawful sublessee/assignee remains
rows.notes: Critical unresolved Unit 1 issue.

rows.label: FEHA classes
rows.value: Race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, genetic information
rows.notes: Includes perception/association.

rows.label: FEHA retaliation
rows.value: Dominant-purpose retaliation/harassment/eviction barred
rows.notes: Source-of-income and aggregate-income rules.

rows.label: Exemption notices
rows.value: Required written notice for single-family/condo exemption; REIT/corporate/LLC limits
rows.notes: AB 1482 notice language.

rows.label: Damages
rows.value: Injunctive relief, excess rent, attorney fees, up to treble for willful/oppressive/fraud/malice
rows.notes: State court enforcement; Rent Board cannot enforce state law.

rows.label: Retaliation - 180-day bar
rows.value: If the landlord retaliates and the tenant is not in default in rent, rent/service changes are restricted within 180 days of the latest applicable enumerated tenantability event: good-faith notice/oral complaint to the landlord, bed-bug notice, qualifying recorded agency complaint, related inspection/citation, proceeding or adverse decision
rows.notes: Subdivision (a) may not be invoked more than once in 12 months. Subdivision (d) separately bars retaliation for organizing/lawful rights; (g) preserves lawful cause stated in good faith in the notice/pleading, subject to proof. Case timing is unverified.

rows.label: Retaliation - organizing and lawful rights
rows.value: Increasing rent to retaliate because a tenant organized or participated in a tenants' association, or lawfully exercised rights, is unlawful
rows.notes: The tenant bears the burden of producing evidence under this subdivision.

rows.label: Retaliation remedies
rows.value: Actual damages; $100-$2,000 punitive damages per retaliatory act only where fraud, oppression or malice is shown; in an action for damages for retaliatory eviction, reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party if requested upon initiation
rows.notes: Civil Code 1942.5(h)-(j); other statutory/decisional remedies are preserved. Not an automatic fee award for every rent-increase dispute.

rows.label: AB 1482 two-unit owner-occupied exemption
rows.value: Exempt only for a two-unit structure in a single building where the owner occupied one unit as a principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU
rows.notes: Owner occupancy of a unit here was not supplied; no exemption asserted (F34).

rows.label: AB 1482 separate-parcel exemption conditions
rows.value: Requires written tenant notice in the statutory form AND that the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member
rows.notes: An individual owner can meet the owner test, but the notice is still required.

rows.label: The 2023 state law: SB 567 (Stats. 2023, Ch. 290)
rows.value: Civil Code Sec. 1947.12's own history note reads '(in Sec. 3) and added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 290, Sec. 4. (SB 567) Effective January 1, 2024. Operative April 1, 2024. Repealed as of January 1, 2030, by its own provisions.'; the Rent Board's AB 1482 page says AB 1482 'is amended by SB 567'
rows.notes: This is the California law passed in 2023 that a reader is most likely to have encountered. It changed the state cap and just-cause framework - it did not create a duty to notify the San Francisco Rent Board of a rent increase.

rows.label: Does any state law reviewed require telling a rent board about a rent increase?
rows.value: No. Read in full on 2026-11-13, Civil Code Sec. 1946.2 (just cause), Sec. 1947.12 (cap), Sec. 827 (notice), Sec. 1942.5 (retaliation) and Sec. 1947.7 (substantial compliance with a local rent program) contain no requirement that an owner notify, file with, or obtain permission from a rent board or any other agency before imposing a rent increase. Sec. 1947.12(e) requires only notice to the tenant under Sec. 827
rows.notes: The Rent Board reporting/licence duty is local (Sec. 37.15). Scope limit: this is a review of the named sections plus the SF pages, not an exhaustive search of the California Codes - see flag F55.

rows.label: State backstop if a local filing was late: Civil Code Sec. 1947.7
rows.value: Intent is 'to limit the imposition of penalties and sanctions against an owner of residential rental units where that person has attempted in good faith to fully comply with the regulatory processes' of a local rent program. An owner in substantial compliance with a rent-control ordinance 'which requires the registration of rents' 'shall not be assessed a penalty or any other sanction for noncompliance', with restitution to the tenant or recovery of registration/filing fees as the exclusive remedies; and 'all annual rent adjustments which may have been denied during the period of the owner's noncompliance shall be restored prospectively once the owner is in compliance'
rows.notes: Do not rely on it yet: SF's ordinance states the Housing Inventory is NOT a rental registry within the meaning of Sections 1947.7-1947.8, so its application to the SF licence scheme is unsettled (Q-24, flag F56). Locally, Rule 13.14 separately preserves the right to re-impose an increase voided for lack of a licence.
